script.base: Chicago is a 3-point home favorite in a 51 total, so implied totals are about CHI 27 and NE 24: a one-score game, not a blowout. Both teams have to throw to get there. Chicago can still lean D.Swift (40 carries, 145 yards over the last 3) and K.Monangai (30/146) if they are up a score late; New England's D.Maye stays pass-lean because 24 implied points plus a 42% Bears blitz will not let them just hand the ball to R.Stevenson.
script.flip1: Chicago jumps ahead early, clocks it with Swift and Monangai, and C.Loveland/R.Odunze/L.Burden receiving yards stall. New England falls behind, abandons the run, and Stevenson (40/147) and T.Henderson (25/95) rush lines die while short targets (H.Henry, E.Raridon, Stevenson) stay alive.
script.flip2: Shootout toward 51: both QBs throw, middle-of-field targets clear, and NE TEs plus CHI featured receivers hit together. A slog/weather under is the other flip, but no forecast is in the pack.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone charting are not in the pack. Location proxy: CHI allows 12.18 YPA in the middle (33 att) vs 6.94 left (64 att) and 7.91 right (66 att). NE allows 11.87 middle (38 att) vs 6.59 left (81) and 5.28 right (72).
matchup.pressure: CHI blitzes 42%. Maye EPA/dropback is 0.11 vs blitz (n=65) vs 0.21 unblitzed, so pressure should cut deep yards and lift TE/RB checkdowns. NE blitzes 35%. C.Williams is the opposite case: 0.16 EPA vs blitz (n=88) vs 0.05 unblitzed, so New England pressure does not force the same checkdown script.
matchup.bleeds: CHI run defense allows 4.58 YPC and 14 runs of 10+, plus 19 passes of 20+ on 183 attempts. NE run defense allows 4.01 YPC and 14 runs of 10+, but only 15 passes of 20+ on 206 attempts. Both secondaries bleed the middle; NE is the tighter explosive defense and is strong to the right.
matchup.overlap: Henry is the overlap: 14 targets, only 66 air yards (about 4.7 aDOT), 154 receiving yards, into the zone where Chicago allows 12.18 YPA, with a 42% blitz pushing Maye short. Raridon (10 targets, 66 air yards, 80 rec yds, about 6.6 aDOT) is the same area as TE2. Burden (20 targets, 183 air, 205 yards) is featured but his air yards may not be the middle, and NE's 15/206 explosive rate argues against chasing him.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Henry is the short-middle answer to a Bears defense allowing 12.18 yards per attempt up the middle, and he has 154 receiving yards in three games (about 51 a game) against a 35-yard line, with Chicago's 42% blitz and Maye's 0.11 EPA when blitzed pushing throws to the TE.
edge_players.must_be_true: Game stays competitive or New England trails so Maye keeps dropping back; Henry holds the 14-target role ahead of Raridon; he is active, which this pack cannot confirm.
edge_players.kills_it: New England leads big and runs Stevenson/Henderson/Kiner; Henry is limited and Raridon takes the middle; Chicago takes the middle away and Maye is forced outside into the 6.9-7.9 YPA zones.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Raridon has shared the same short middle (10 targets, 66 air yards, 80 receiving yards, about 27 a game) and 15.5 is well under that role if Chicago's 42% blitz and 12.18 middle YPA keep New England throwing underneath while trailing or staying within a score.
edge_players.must_be_true: He keeps a real route share alongside Henry, as in the last three games, and New England does not turn this into a pure run clock.
edge_players.kills_it: Henry monopolizes the TE targets; New England leads and runs; Raridon is inactive or a healthy scratch the pack does not show.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig is in the pack, so step 8 cannot price the edge and nothing here should be treated as a 70%+ leg. Henry: 154/3=51.3 vs 35 agrees with the middle-YPA and blitz read, but the listed price is +nan, so the 35 may not be a real offer — flag that to the human, do not size it. Raridon: 80/3=26.7 vs 15.5 at -115 agrees on form; same-game cannibalization with Henry is the disagreeing piece, so this stays a lean not a strong. Not used: Burden 205/3=68.3 vs 57.5 dies if Chicago leads and runs; Odunze 57.7 vs 44.5 fights NE's 15/206 explosive rate; Swift rush 48.3 vs 61.5 and rush+rec 72.3 vs 86.5 are under recent form but the -3 script pushes the other way; Stevenson rush+rec 195/3=65.0 vs 65.5 is a push; Kiner 6.4 ypc and Maye 8.5 ypc look fluky; A.Brown 27 yards vs a 70 line with no price looks like a bad mapping, not a bet.

market_rung_price: Receiving yards is the allowed market (receptions would fit the checkdown read but are disallowed). Henry recyds over 35 — price not in pack (+nan); do not take a rung until a book posts a number near the main line. Raridon recyds over 15.5 -115, main line only, no alt. Do not add passing yards or TDs.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because Chicago's 42% blitz turned into incompletions, not checkdowns: Maye's EPA falls to 0.11 when blitzed, Doubs (221 air yards) and Douglas (180 air) took the shots, and Henry's 154 yards were YAC a coverage shell we do not have charted took away — or Henry was a late inactive. Raridon under 15.5 is the cleaner miss if Henry simply hogged the 14-target TE role and Raridon' s 80 yards were a three-game share that did not show up in one game. That cannibalization case is real, which is why Raridon is a lean, but it is not stronger than 27 vs 15.5 in a dog-trailing script. The favorite-runs-the-clock flip hurts Chicago receivers, not these two.
slip_story: One story: New England throwing underneath into Chicago's middle (12.18 YPA) in a 51-point game, including the flip where CHI -3 leads and NE is chasing. Henry over and Raridon over win together on that script. Do not add a game under, and do not add Swift/Stevenson rush overs — those need the clock-killing run script that cuts this passing tree. Burden/Odunze overs need Chicago to keep throwing and die on the favorite-leads flip, so they stay off this slip.
